topology_reasoning.device_identification: Symmetric three-waveguide adiabatic/trident coupler. A wide center stem narrows to a terminating tip while two disconnected outer rails begin as narrow tips, broaden through the same interaction region, and then fan out to two parallel output guides.
topology_reasoning.operating_principle: The long counter-tapered three-guide region transfers the center-stem mode into the two symmetric outer supermodes. The outer S-bends then increase port separation without changing guide width.

observed_geometry.center_stem: Runs from the left edge to about x=25.1 um and tapers from about 0.27 um to a narrow terminating tip.
observed_geometry.outer_interaction_rails: Begin around x=3.04 um at roughly 0.07 um width and taper to about 0.244 um near x=25.5 um.
observed_geometry.interaction_offsets: Outer centerlines remain near +/-0.27 um through the counter-taper region.
observed_geometry.fanout: Begins near x=26 um, follows mirrored smooth S-bends, and reaches output center offsets near +/-0.73 um by about x=36 um.
observed_geometry.output_guides: Two parallel rails of about 0.244 um width continue to the right footprint edge.

topology_reasoning.implementation_plan: Build three disconnected primitive paths on layer (1,0): one straight center path with a linear width taper, plus two mirrored outer paths whose width linearly increases over the straight interaction segment and remains constant over a cubic-Bezier S-bend and straight output segment.

iterations.change_made: Initial calibrated primitive model: linear counter-tapers, mirrored cosine S-bend fanout, and exact 40.0 x 1.7 um footprint. The diff showed a small vertical centerline bias in the interaction region, but the IoU stop threshold was already exceeded, so no further comparison iteration was run.

knob_response.width_basis: Mean physical width of the linearly tapered center guide.

final.export_note: GDS metadata was disabled after scoring so verify_knob_response sees the real top cell. The three layer-(1,0) polygon coordinates and their SHA-256 geometry signature were identical before and after this packaging-only change.
